target_statement: Determine the full degree-at-most-two inverse-form spaces for every rank-three irreducible quadric relative to a hyperplane, then prove support containment only when the Pfaffian equation also permits it.
implication_to_classification: An exhaustive pair-normal-form calculation reduces the intrinsic H+2Q stratum with rank(Q)=3 to explicitly retained finite coefficient equations; a kernel computation alone is not coverage.
coefficient_ring: QQ[y0,y1,y2,y3]; all 90 coefficients of alpha and all 20 affine beta coefficients, with no specialization of Poisson parameters.
hypotheses: Q is an irreducible projective rank-three quadric; the hyperplane either does not contain its vertex, contains the vertex and is transverse to the quotient conic, or is tangent to that conic. Inverse closedness is Q*dalpha-2*dQ wedge alpha=0, and Pf(alpha)=k*Q^2 with k nonzero remains compulsory.
inverted_elements: Q only in the rational inverse form; k nonzero for generic rank four
complements: All Q=0 points remain governed by polynomial identities.
Rank-two or lower quadrics and other degeneracy divisor types are outside this job.
success_certificate: Exact QQ kernel and primitive-image dimensions for all three cases; separately constructed polynomial matrices and all composition identities, followed by explicit proofs or a fully stated remaining Pfaffian problem.
independent_check: SymPy exterior-form matrix construction using symbolic derivatives, independent of legacy sparse polynomial arithmetic; exact rank and residual-form comparison.
negative_result_next_step: Retain any extra inverse-form classes and unresolved Pfaffian branches; do not infer primitive exactness or coverage from a nearby rank-four case. Stop coefficient expansion if no geometric implication follows.
